text:
maria: Heads-up — I ran a microbenchmark across our GA fleet after vendorX driver 2.4.0 landed. Seeing a ~18% tail latency bump for long-sequence chat when FlashPaged is selected. Noting it only happens when batch_size >= 8 and kv_cache is enabled.

devon: Can you paste the commands and numbers?

maria: command I used: `bench/attn_bench --model redwood/ggml-8b --seq 2048 --bs 8 --kernels flashpaged,flashv2,paged`

Results summary (p50/p95 p99 in ms):
- flashv2: 32 / 78 / 210
- flashpaged: 40 / 95 / 248  <-- regression after vendorX 2.4.0
- paged: 38 / 86 / 230

maria: Profile flamegraphs show much higher memcpy and small kernel launches in flashpaged path when kv_cache hits occur. Attaching wave of perf annotations: `cpu: memcpy 34% -> kernel-launch overhead up`

lee: Weird — flashpaged was supposed to reduce KV pressure. Is it possible vendorX changed small kernel scheduling?

sophia: vLLM recently shipped a scheduler tweak in v0.8.2 that changes how async CUDA streams are used. Any chance our pinned vLLM/xformers combo is interacting?

maria: Good call. I pulled upstream commits:
- flash-attn repo: v1.3.1 -> v1.4.0 includes `fast-launch` change (PR #412)
- vLLM: we are on 0.8.1; upstream 0.8.2 has a stream-affinity patch (PR #89)
- xFormers: no change in kernels but a recent fallback path (PR #220) toggles fused kernels on certain SMs

devon: Could be a three-way: vendor driver scheduling + FA fast-launch + vLLM stream affinity. Any repro on a single machine?

maria: Repro'd on a single-gpu devbox (A100 equivalent), reproduced after driver upgrade. Reverted driver -> perf returns. So vendor driver seems necessary condition.

lee: Do we see correctness regressions or just perf?

maria: No outputs changed. It's strictly perf.

eng-runtime-bot: Deployment note: rolling canary of kernel-selection heuristic scheduled for 2026-03-18 03:00 UTC per RFC 1023.

sophia: For short-term mitigation, we can change kernel selection policy: if seq >= 1024 and bs >= 8 and kv_cache=true, prefer `paged` over `flashpaged`. That should avoid the weird launch pattern.

devon: Agreed. Also add a CI microbenchmark that runs flashpaged with kv enabled on our smallest canary to detect regressions on driver bumps.

maria: I prepared a quick heuristic patch to runtime routing:
```
if (kernel == FLASHPAGED && kv_enabled && batch >= 8 && seq >= 1024 && driver_version >= "2.4.0") {
  select(PAGED);
}
```
I'll put up a draft PR.

sophia: Add a flag so we can flip it server-side without redeploying clients.

maria: PR link: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/879 (draft). It includes perf numbers and a perftest that runs nightly.

lee: Can someone open issues upstream? We should file minimal repro and ask FA maintainers if they changed block-size heuristics. I'll ping @fa-maintainer and vendorX.

maria: Filed:
- flash-attn issue 515 with repro + flamegraph (https://github.com/flash-attn/issues/515)
- vendorX driver ticket #9876 with perf profile
- vLLM: noted their stream-affinity PR in case of interaction

sophia: Long-term: look into batching heuristic that probes small batches before committing to flashpaged path (cheap trial run). Could avoid tail regressions. Add to roadmap.

devon: Also track fallback policy: if we detect >10% p95 drift vs baseline in canary, auto-switch to fallback kernel for that model/version to restore SLO.

maria: OK, next steps: 1) land heuristic PR as draft toggle (maria) 2) add nightly microbench and CI alert (devon) 3) open upstream threads and monitor (lee) 4) add canary auto-fallback rule (sophia). I'll update this thread with PR and perf numbers after deploy.

lee: Thanks — nice triage. :thumbsup:

maria: quick addendum: fused-attention microbench (fused kernels) didn't show the same behavior; this looks specific to the paged+flash hybrid. Fused still recommended for shorter sequences.

eng-runtime-bot: Canary rollout started 2026-03-18 03:05 UTC — monitoring alerts enabled.

maria: Alert triggered on canary: p95 up 12% on canary instances using flashpaged. Patch flip to paged executed, metrics returned to baseline.

sophia: Great. Leave the toggle in place until upstream fixes or vendor patches. We'll schedule an explainer in next eng-runtime sync.

maria: End of thread — saving logs to /artifacts/perf/1935678901/ and closing ticket if no further regressions after 72h.
